concepts.def: Meeting needs without harming future generations.
The demand humans place on nature.
Designing out waste and reusing materials.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Sustainability — a core area of A-Level Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Sustainability brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Sustainability.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which cycle has no significant atmospheric phase?
options: Carbon
Nitrogen
Phosphorus
Sulfur

mcqs.q: Average time in a reservoir is called?
options: Flux
Residence time
Lifetime
Half-life

mcqs.q: What does the 'tragedy of the commons' describe?
options: It is a play about poor people.
The size a species can reach.
Shared resources tend to be overexploited because individuals benefit personally while sharing costs.
Common land in medieval Britain.

mcqs.q: Why is burning fossil fuels considered to disrupt the carbon cycle?
options: Common land in medieval Britain.
It removes carbon permanently.
It releases carbon stored for millions of years much faster than the cycle can absorb.
It creates new carbon that did not exist before.
The maximum population an environment can sustainably support given available resources.
It removes carbon permanently.
How much an animal can physically carry.
The size a species can reach.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Biogeochemical cycle”?
options: Average time an element spends in a reservoir = reservoir size / flux.
Slow, sedimentary cycle: weathering of rocks releases phosphate; runs through life and back to ocean sediments.
Pathway by which a chemical element moves through biotic and abiotic compartments of Earth.
Human alteration of natural fluxes (e.g., Haber process doubled global reactive N input).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Reservoir”?
options: Human alteration of natural fluxes (e.g., Haber process doubled global reactive N input).
Compartment storing a quantity of an element, e.g., ocean carbon, soil nitrogen.
Pathway by which a chemical element moves through biotic and abiotic compartments of Earth.
Includes volcanic outgassing, biological reduction (DMS) and atmospheric oxidation to sulfate aerosols.
